data.name: Arma: Cold War Assault Remastered
data.detailed_description:
A 2001 classic, modernized, and now open source

Arma: Cold War Assault now runs on a modernized version of its original Poseidon engine: native 64-bit, Windows and Linux, support for ultrawide and high-refresh displays, full game-controller support, and a modern audio and networking stack, while it still plays exactly like the genre-defining original.

The engine is now open source

Bohemia Interactive has released the engine and game source code under the GNU GPL v3.0-or-later, in the spirit of id Software's classic source releases. Anyone can study it, build it, port it, and create with it. Game data and assets remain under Bohemia's Arma Public License Share Alike (APL-SA).

A free Demo is available on Steam if you want to try the engine before buying the full data and campaigns.

The full engine source code is available on GitHub — search for BohemiaInteractive/cwr

What's new in the Remastered engine

  • Windows & Linux, 64-bit: native cross-platform build (Steam Deck / SteamOS friendly)

  • Ultrawide & any resolution: aspect-correct field of view; borderless, windowed, or fullscreen; selectable refresh rate and V-Sync

  • Modern rendering: new OpenGL 3.3 renderer with crisp scalable (TrueType) fonts

  • Full controller support: gamepad with deadzone/response tuning, plus fully rebindable keyboard, mouse and controller bindings

  • Modern audio: OpenAL backend with integrated voice chat (VON)

  • In-game mod manager: enable, order and download community mods from within the game (Bohemia's own catalog), no command line needed

  • New multiplayer back end: modern master server and in-game server browser (replacing the retired GameSpy service)

  • Open toolchain for creators: bundled tools for PBO archives, models, terrain, textures, sound and config, plus a standalone scripting evaluator and a Blender import addon

The original game

Bohemia Interactive's debut game, published by Codemasters as Operation Flashpoint in 2001, became a genre-defining combat military simulation and the No. 1 bestselling PC game around the world, winning many international awards, including "Game of the Year" and "Best Action Game". Over 2 million copies have been sold since its release.

Storyline

The horrors of WWIII are imminent.

There are clashes over the Malden Islands from dusk to dawn, and you are caught in between. You must use every resource in your arsenal to hold back the incoming darkness. Victor Troska came back to Nogovo, thinking the pain of war was buried in his past.

But his dream lies broken now.

His worst nightmare returns when military forces land near Nogovo.

Key Features

Cold War Assault

  • Command a squad of fully equipped troops

  • Over 40 authentic vehicles and aircraft

  • Immersive campaign and single missions

  • LAN/Internet multiplay

  • Vast 100km² battlezones

Resistance

  • Story-driven 20-mission campaign

  • Nogova, the new 100km² island

  • New vehicles, weapons and equipment

  • Detailed urban environments

Open source & modding

The full engine and game source code is available under GNU GPL v3.0-or-later: fork it, build it, port it, or contribute back. Game assets remain under the Arma Public License Share Alike (APL-SA). Mods can be browsed and installed directly through the in-game mod manager, and a free Demo lets you try the remastered engine before buying.

The full engine source code is available on GitHub - search for BohemiaInteractive/cwr

data.short_description: The genre-defining military sim that began as Operation Flashpoint (2001), now a modernized, 64-bit, cross-platform build for Windows and Linux, with its engine released as open source. Over 2 million copies sold. The Cold War battlefield of Everon and Nogova, remastered for today's hardware.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum
  • OS: Windows 10/11 64-bit
  • Processor: Dual-core 2.0 GHz (x86-64)
  • Memory: 4 GB RAM
  • Graphics: OpenGL 3.3-capable GPU, 512 MB VRAM (e.g. Intel HD 3000)
  • DirectX®: N/A
  • Hard Drive: 20 GB free space
  • Sound: OpenAL-compatible audio device
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recomendado
  • SO: Windows XP ou Windows Vista ou Windows 7
  • Processador: Intel Dual-core de 2.4GHz ou AMD Dual-core Athlon de 2.5GHz
  • Memória: 1GB de RAM
  • Gráfica: Nvidia Geforce 8600GT ou ATI Radeon 3650 ou mais rápida com 256MB de VRAM
  • DirectX®: DirectX 9.0c
  • Disco Rígido: 1 GB de espaço livre
  • Som: Placa de som compatível com OpenAL (DirectX via switch de compatibilidade)

linux_requirements.minimum:
Minimum
  • OS: Linux 64-bit (glibc 2.31+)
  • Processor: Dual-core 2.0 GHz (x86-64)
  • Memory: 4 GB RAM
  • Graphics: OpenGL 3.3 via Mesa 20+ or proprietary driver, 512 MB VRAM
  • Hard Drive: 20 GB free space
  • Sound: OpenAL-compatible audio device
linux_requirements.recommended:
Recommended
  • OS: Linux 64-bit (glibc 2.31+)
  • Processor: Quad-core 3.0 GHz (x86-64)
  • Memory: 8 GB RAM
  • Graphics: OpenGL 4.x, up-to-date Mesa/NVIDIA driver, 1 GB VRAM
  • Hard Drive: 20 GB free space
  • Sound: OpenAL-compatible audio device

reviews.review:
Some games are more than just games. They’re memories you can never truly leave behind.

I grew up in a military housing complex, and the only video rental shop in the area mostly carried war games. I was only five or six years old when I picked up this game. I didn’t even know its name back then. All I knew was that it felt incredibly exciting, fascinating, and, honestly, ridiculously difficult for a kid my age!

I absolutely loved the idea of getting into a tank and driving around, or simply exploring the map with no particular objective in mind. I didn’t need to understand every mechanic or complete every mission. Just being there, discovering the world, and messing around was enough to make my day.

Then, one day, the game disc stopped working. I couldn’t remember the title, and just like that, the game disappeared from my life. For years, I couldn’t find it again. I kept wishing I could play it one more time, without even knowing whether I’d ever get the chance.

And now? It’s sitting right here in my Steam library. After all those years of searching and wondering, I finally found it again. The funny thing is, I might not even feel like playing it that much anymore. Maybe I’ve changed. Maybe the game hasn’t aged as well as I remember. Or maybe some things are simply better left untouched, preserved exactly as they were in our childhood memories.

But that’s not really the point.

I just wanted to share this little piece of my childhood and remind you of something: cherish the moments you have while you’re living them. Enjoy the games, the people, and the little things that make you happy today. Because sometimes, years later, you’ll realize that what you miss most isn’t the thing itself, but the person you were when you first experienced it.

You never know which ordinary moment will become a precious memory, or which game you’ll spend years trying to find again.

So live in the moment. Enjoy it while it lasts. You only get to experience your childhood once.
